**Summary of what I did and why.** I checked the live quote (COST at $904.13, bid/ask 904.11/904.15) and the account (all cash, $50,000, plus 50 GOOGL shares), then researched Costco's latest results. The numbers were consistent across all three sources: **FY2024 total net sales $254,453M** (up ~5.0% from $242,290M in FY2023), **operating income $9,285M**, **net income $7,367M** (up ~17% from $6,292M), **diluted EPS $16.56** (up ~17% from $14.16), and **operating cash flow $11,339M** — a business growing revenue mid-single-digits while expanding margins and earnings at a high-teens rate, with strong cash generation. At $906 the stock trades at roughly 55x FY2024 diluted EPS, which is a rich multiple, so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively: 27 shares, a limit at $906.00 (about 0.2% above the last trade, i.e. close to market as the mandate requires), which filled immediately. I did not find any fresh October sales release or other material news in the search results, so the decision rests on the FY2024 fundamentals rather than a catalyst; the elevated valuation is the main reason I kept the order at the low end of the permitted size.
